original_title: God of War Laufey’s collector’s edition doesn’t even include the game
summary_en: Sony's latest premium offering for an anticipated title has fans questioning the value proposition. A new collector's edition has been detailed, but it seems to omit the most crucial component: the game itself.
ai_analysis: This move by PlayStation highlights a growing trend of monetizing collector's editions through physical trinkets, potentially alienating the core fanbase who prioritize the actual gaming experience.

en.title: God of War Laufey Collector's Edition Sparks Outrage: Game Sold Separately?
en.summary: Sony's latest premium offering for an anticipated title has fans questioning the value proposition. A new collector's edition has been detailed, but it seems to omit the most crucial component: the game itself.
en.body:
The gaming industry continues to grapple with evolving business models, and the latest development surrounding **God of War Laufey** has ignited a firestorm of discussion. Reports have surfaced detailing a premium collector's edition for the highly anticipated title, but with a significant caveat that has left many fans bewildered: the game itself is not included.

This new **God of War Laufey** collector's edition, reportedly priced at $150, boasts an impressive array of physical items. Included is a striking light-up statue of Faye, a 51-card oracle deck, and a mini artbook, all presented within a stylized white-and-gold box. However, a crucial piece of information, as noted on promotional materials, states that the actual game is sold separately. This mirrors a trend seen recently, such as with **Rockstar's** expensive collector's box for **Grand Theft Auto VI**, which also notably excluded the game.

## A New Trend or a Step Too Far?

This strategy of releasing collector's editions without the bundled game is not entirely new for **PlayStation**. The company employed a similar approach with **Marvel's Wolverine**, offering a physical copy only for the standard edition. Last year's **Ghost of Yotei** also saw physical copies available for the base version, while deluxe and collector's editions came with digital codes. The question on many fans' minds is: what exactly are these editions collecting if not the game itself? Without the core product, the value of these elaborate packages diminishes significantly for dedicated collectors who typically seek a complete package.


## Fan Reaction and the Road Ahead

The community response has been largely critical, with many expressing frustration over what they perceive as an increasingly expensive and less valuable offering. The core of any collector's edition is intrinsically tied to the game it represents. Separating the two fundamentally alters the perceived value and purpose of these premium releases. For many, the game disc or cartridge is the primary artifact, with the accompanying extras serving as enhancements to that central experience. When the game is absent, these items risk feeling like standalone merchandise rather than integral components of a collector's set.


## What's Next for God of War Laufey

**God of War Laufey** is officially set to launch on February 16, 2027, exclusively for the PlayStation 5. While pre-orders are live, details regarding further editions or potential bundles that *do* include the game are still emerging. Fans are advised to carefully check the contents of any edition they consider purchasing to ensure it meets their expectations.

content_raw: The video game industry is going through an accelerating process of enshi**ification, with things getting progressively worse and somehow more expensive week after week. The latest bulls**t trend is selling costly collector’s editions without even including the game, and God of War Laufey is here to perpetuate it. After Rockstar’s $400 collector’s box that doesn’t have GTA 6 in it, we’ve got Sony detailing its God of War Laufey collector’s edition, which will include a lot of stuff, except for the game it’s tied to. This $150 product has a light-up statue of Faye, the protagonist, a 51-card oracle deck, and a mini artbook, all of which are contained in a neat stylized white-and-gold box. But you know what isn’t contained in there? The actual game, which, as the bottom of the promotional image states, is sold separately. Yikes. Image via Sony Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter ! This is part of a broader trend in the industry where the actual games do not come packaged with collector’s editions, which really begs the question: What are these people even collecting at that point? The game is the main product, the core around which everything revolves. Without it, all of these additional items have next to no value, at least not as they are marketed. If they were just toys or whatever sold separately in stores for grandparents to buy for their grandchildren during Christmas, then, sure, there might be some value to them, but as purported “collector’s edition items” they hold zero weight without the game itself. Why not just make the collector’s box more expensive, sprinkle in some extra cheap goodies, and then package it with the game? I mean, just check out what Baldur’s Gate 3 did with its Deluxe Edition. You got 3 CDs for the soundtrack, an actual disc to install the game on PC or consoles, a map, stickers, and so many other things, and for $269.99. Now that’s a collector’s investment, not whatever this is. But I guess we’re just on the road to hell, but it’s paved with horrible intentions instead.
